headline: SILVER SURGES 5.22% to $81.19 — Gold-Silver Ratio Contracts to 58.4 as Industrial Bid Accelerates
snippet: Silver posted its sharpest single-session gain in months, hitting $81.19/oz and compressing the gold-to-silver ratio to 58.4 — its tightest reading since mid-April. The white metal is now up more than 150% year-over-year, driven by tightening supply and relentless industrial demand from photovoltaics and EVs, with the Silver Institute projecting a 67-million-ounce structural deficit for 2026.

headline: CHINA SILVER STOCKPILE: 790+ Tonnes Imported in Early 2026 — Gold Producers Still Trade at 10% Valuation Discount
snippet: China's aggressive silver procurement — over 790 tonnes imported in the first months of 2026, partly driven by solar manufacturing — is establishing a strong demand floor beneath spot prices. Gold producers are simultaneously trading at 6.4x 2026E EV/EBITDA, a 10% discount to historical averages, even as realized prices surged to $4,861/oz in Q1 with AISCs near $1,483 — implying record margins still not priced into equities.

headline: ACID ZERO: China's Sulphuric Acid Cutoff Puts 1.1 Million Tonnes of Chilean Copper Annually at Risk
snippet: Chinese customs data shows zero sulphuric acid shipped to Chile last month — down from 151,268 tonnes in March 2025 — threatening the heap-leach operations that produce roughly 20% of Chilean copper output. With Russia extending its own export ban through June, Turkey restricting shipments, and the Strait of Hormuz disrupting Middle East sulphur, miners are now facing acid cost spikes of 40–60% with no easy alternative source.

headline: COPPER WITHIN SIGHT OF ALL-TIME HIGH at $6.23/lb as Chinese Smelters Run at Record Throughput
snippet: Copper futures climbed to $6.23/lb — approaching the record highs set in late January — as Chinese smelters hit record processing rates even as their margins stay compressed. The long-term demand thesis remains intact: AI data center buildout, power grid modernization, and clean energy infrastructure are sustaining the bid, with copper up 35% year-over-year.

headline: SILVER47: 38.7 g/t Gold and 1,713 g/t Silver Returned from 15km Near-Surface Nevada Vein Network
snippet: Silver47 Exploration (TSX-V: AGA) reported rock samples up to 38.7 g/t Au and 1,713 g/t Ag from the expanded Kennedy Gold-Silver Project in Nevada, highlighting a 15km largely untested vein network across the newly expanded 6,150-acre property. A 3,000-sample soil geochemistry grid and induced polarization geophysics are now underway to sharpen drill targets across the priority corridors.

headline: STANDARD URANIUM DRILLS FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2022 — Two Rigs Hit Arrow-Adjacent Corridors in Athabasca
snippet: Standard Uranium (TSX-V: STND) has mobilized two drill rigs to its Davidson River flagship in Saskatchewan's southwest Athabasca Basin, launching the company's first campaign at the property since 2022. The fully-permitted program targets the Warrior, Bronco, and Thunderbird conductor corridors along the same structural trends hosting NexGen Energy's Arrow deposit and Paladin Energy's Triple R.

headline: UR-ENERGY OPENS SECOND ISR URANIUM MINE: Shirley Basin Operational, Q1 Cash Cost Falls 13% to $37.51/lb
snippet: Ur-Energy (NYSE: URG) commenced ISR uranium production at its Shirley Basin project in Wyoming in April — its second operating mine — while reporting Q1 2026 cash costs of $37.51/lb, down 13% from Q4 2025. April production hit 57,479 lbs, the highest monthly output since 2023, as the company sold Q1 uranium at an average of $70.98/lb against a market spot price still searching for direction.

headline: JOHN FENECK: Gold Stock Weakness Is the Setup — Producer Cash Flow Surge Points to Coming M&A Wave
snippet: Analyst John Feneck argues the persistent underperformance of gold equities against $4,700+ bullion is creating acquisition targets — not a reason to avoid the sector. With producers generating free cash flow at record margins (Agnico Eagle realized $4,861/oz vs. $1,483 AISC in Q1), Feneck sees cashed-up seniors shopping for junior and mid-tier assets in the second half of 2026.

headline: LITHIUM DEFICIT INCOMING: Energy Storage Demand Up 71% in 2025, Morgan Stanley Sees 80,000-Tonne Flip by Year-End
snippet: The energy storage boom is on track to flip the lithium market from a 61,000-tonne surplus in 2025 to an 80,000-tonne deficit in 2026, according to Morgan Stanley — with UBS estimating a more conservative 22,000-tonne gap. Battery storage is projected to grow another 55% this year, pushing its share of total lithium demand from 23% to 31%, as the SQM-Codelco partnership ramps Chilean output 25% by volume in Q1.

headline: NDPR TUMBLES 21% IN APRIL to $99.61/kg — Still 88% Above January as China Quota Watch Begins
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide posted its steepest monthly decline since the Q1 rally, falling 21% in April to $99.61/kg — but still sits well above the cost bases of MP Materials and Lynas. Markets are consolidating ahead of China's mid-year MIIT mining quota announcement (typically June), which analysts expect to be the next directional trigger for the rare earth complex.
